title: The water cycle in a glass valley

bodies.name: Mountains
bodies.label: Mountains
bodies.describe: Air forced up their slopes expands and cools.

bodies.name: Lake
bodies.label: Lake · source of vapour
bodies.describe: Sunlight gives water molecules the energy to escape as vapour.

bodies.name: Water vapour
bodies.label: Water vapour
bodies.describe: Invisible gas in reality; drawn here as rising motes.

bodies.name: Cloud
bodies.label: Cloud · condensed droplets
bodies.describe: Vapour condenses on dust into droplets; the cloud darkens as it fills.

bodies.name: Wind
bodies.label: Wind
bodies.describe: Carries the cloud west, towards the mountains.

bodies.name: Rain
bodies.label: Rain
bodies.describe: Falls when the cloud holds more water than its air can keep suspended.

bodies.name: Sun
bodies.label: Sun · the energy source
bodies.describe: Its height through the day sets how strongly the lake is heated.

lessons.title: Heat the lake
lessons.text: Turn the sun up. Watch the vapour rise faster above the lake and the humidity readout climb: evaporation needs energy.
lessons.explain: Each molecule that leaves takes its latent heat with it; more heating means a higher evaporation rate.

lessons.title: Let the wind carry the cloud
lessons.text: With a steady wind the cloud drifts west. Follow it to the mountains and wait for the rain event.
lessons.explain: Rising over the slopes the air expands and cools; the saturation vapour pressure falls below the vapour actually present, so the excess condenses onto droplets, which grow until they fall as rain.

lessons.title: Calm air
lessons.text: Drop the wind almost to zero. The cloud now stays over the lake and keeps filling until it rains back where it came from.
lessons.explain: Without transport the cycle closes locally: evaporation, condensation and rain over the same water.

lessons.title: Evening
lessons.text: Move the time of day to evening. With the sun low, heating falls and so does evaporation.
lessons.explain: The energy input sets the pace of the whole cycle.
